claim: Amazon allows a wide range of branded and generic products, but some require permission from the brand or Amazon first.
evidence: though in some cases you may need to get permission from a brand or Amazon first.

claim: Resellers should obtain products from a legitimate source, such as a wholesale supplier or manufacturer.
evidence: Obtain the products from a legitimate source, like a wholesale supplier or manufacturer.

claim: Resellers should check that a product is safe and complies with the laws of the countries where it is sold.
evidence: Also, check that the product is safe, and that it complies with laws and regulations for the countries

claim: In some cases a reseller can match an offer to a brand's existing listing.
evidence: in some cases you can match an offer to a brand's existing product listing in the Amazon store.

claim: Matching starts from Catalog > Add Products in Seller Central.
evidence: Hover over Catalog in the main menu of Seller Central, then select Add Products.

claim: The reseller selects a product condition from a dropdown menu.
evidence: Use the dropdown menu to select a product condition.

claim: Products that require approval show an Apply to sell button.
evidence: If the product requires approval, you'll see an Apply to sell button.

claim: Products that require brand approval prompt a Selling application for Brand.
evidence: If the product requires brand approval, you'll be prompted to complete a Selling application for Brand.

claim: The application needs a purchase invoice from a manufacturer or distributor.
evidence: you will need to provide a purchase invoice that you received from a manufacturer or distributor

claim: Alternatively, the application can use a brand authorization letter.
evidence: or a brand authorization letter.

claim: A brand authorization letter comes directly from the brand and authorizes you to sell its products.
evidence: A brand authorization letter is a letter directly from a brand that authorizes you to sell their products.

claim: The letter must be dated within 180 days.
evidence: Is dated within 180 days

claim: The letter must include your name and address, matching your Amazon selling account.
evidence: Includes your name and address, matching the information in your Amazon selling account

claim: The letter must be on the brand's letterhead with the brand's name and address.
evidence: Is on the brand’s letterhead, and includes the name and address of the brand

claim: The letter must be a high-resolution PDF in the correct orientation.
evidence: Is a high-resolution PDF file in the correct orientation

claim: Matching an existing listing does not let you create new product detail pages for a brand enrolled in Brand Registry.
evidence: this approach doesn't provide you with the ability to create new product detail pages for a brand enrolled in Brand Registry
verifier_note: Added the source's condition (brand enrolled in Brand Registry).

claim: A seller with an agreement with a brand can ask the brand to assign a Reseller role in Brand Registry.
evidence: you can contact them to ask that they assign you a Reseller role in Brand Registry.

claim: The Reseller role grants selling privileges including the ability to create new product detail pages.
evidence: This grants you certain selling privileges and benefits, including the ability to create new product detail pages.

claim: The Reseller role is for external third-party sellers authorized to sell a brand's goods.
evidence: The Reseller role is for external, third-party sellers who are authorized to sell a brand's goods and services.

claim: The Reseller role unlocks brand selling benefits on a limited basis.
evidence: unlocks brand selling benefits, but on a limited basis.

claim: The Reseller role does not grant access to Brand Analytics.
evidence: doesn't grant access to Brand Analytics

claim: A selling account can have only one role (Reseller or Brand Representative).
evidence: You can only have one role per selling account (Reseller or Brand Representative).
verifier_note: Source does not say 'per brand'; page wording corrected.

claim: When a brand connects another seller's account, it provides that seller's merchant token, a unique identifier the seller finds in its selling account.
evidence: provide a merchant token for the seller. A merchant token is a unique identifier that the seller can find in their selling account.
verifier_note: Added the invitation context from the source so the page's use of the token is supported.

claim: To receive a role invitation, the contact must first have a Brand Registry account.
evidence: Note that to receive an invitation, the contact must first have a Brand Registry account.

claim: A brand Administrator can invite as many selling accounts as it likes.
evidence: If you have the brand Administrator role, you can invite as many selling accounts as you'd like.

claim: Amazon advises assigning protection roles only to employee or other internal accounts.
evidence: Only assign protection roles to employee accounts, or other accounts internal to the brand.

claim: The Brand Representative role is for first-party sellers directly employed by the brand.
evidence: The Brand Representative role is for internal, first-party sellers who are directly employed by the brand.

claim: A+ Content is open to sellers with a Brand Representative or Reseller role for an enrolled brand.
evidence: You also need a Brand Representative or Reseller role assigned to a brand enrolled in Amazon Brand Registry,

claim: Vine is open to sellers with a Brand Representative or Reseller role for an enrolled brand.
evidence: a Brand Representative or Reseller role assigned to a brand enrolled in Amazon Brand Registry

claim: Transparency assigns a unique code to every unit of an enrolled product.
evidence: The Amazon Transparency program uses serialization technology to assign a unique code to every unit of an enrolled product.

claim: Once products are fully protected by Transparency, they cannot be listed in Transparency-supported stores without valid Transparency codes that match the enrolled product.
evidence: Once your products are fully protected by Transparency, they cannot be listed in Amazon's Transparency-supported stores without valid Transparency codes
verifier_note: Added the source's condition ('once fully protected').

claim: Amazon says Transparency codes help verify that only authentic items are shipped to customers, whether orders are fulfilled by Amazon or shipped directly by the brand.
evidence: verify that only authentic, accurate items are shipped to customers, ... whether orders are fulfilled by Amazon or shipped directly by you.
verifier_note: In the source 'you' is the enrolled brand and the sentence is about verifying authenticity, not a listing rule for resellers' own shipments; narrowed.

claim: All units must have a valid Transparency code, either Amazon-issued or an existing serial code connected to Transparency, or they will not pass the Transparency check.
evidence: All units must have a valid Amazon Transparency code—either Amazon-issued or an existing serial code connected to Transparency—or they won't pass

claim: An invitation to a selling role is sent to the seller by email.
evidence: This will send an invitation to the seller via email.
